messages:
elaine: started the RBAC roles/schema refactor canary at 18:02 UTC. small percentage of users routed to canary. seeing a spike of 'access denied to KMS key' errors from production: `kms.decrypt` failing. any immediate ideas?
kevin: noticed a batch of service accounts lost the 'kms-access' role after the roleset prune step. possibly an over-aggressive default-role cleanup.
miguel: copying relevant logs: `ERROR org.redwood.kms KMS_ACCESS_DENIED project=redwood-prod key=projects/..../keys/primary svcacct=svc-infer-01@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
mira: @oncall can you pause the migration job? I think we should stop before the next chunk.
oncall: migration job pause command executed by mira. job id: rbac-schema-v3-canary-18. queued tasks halted. (runbooks: /runbooks/rbac-migrations.md)
els: quick sanity check: how many principals lost kms role? I ran a query: 
```
-- count principals without explicit kms-access after prune
SELECT count(*) FROM principals p WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM role_assignments r WHERE r.principal_id = p.id AND r.role = 'kms-access'
) AND p.type = 'service_account';
```
result: 42 service accounts affected in canary shard.
kevin: that aligns with the errors. looks like default-role removal removed 'legacy-kms'->'kms-access' mapping for some SA rows with null role_map_version. migration script assumed role_map_version non-null. bug.
miguel: local repro: run the pruning SQL with `WHERE role_map_version IS NOT NULL` fixed things. propose a targeted backfill for the affected principal ids before resuming.
mira: agree. we should also patch the migration to not touch principals with null role_map_version and add a data backfill step.
elain: action plan: 1) run targeted SQL to reapply kms-access for the 42 SAs; 2) patch migration and smoke test on canary; 3) hold rollout until SLO for KMS errors stable for 1 hour.
kevin: here's the backfill SQL I will run in read-committed transaction (will attach to runbook):
```
BEGIN;
UPDATE role_assignments r SET role = 'kms-access', updated_by = 'rbac-mgr'
WHERE r.principal_id IN ( /* list extracted from earlier query */ ) AND r.role IS DISTINCT FROM 'kms-access';
INSERT INTO role_assignments (principal_id, role, created_by)
SELECT p.id, 'kms-access', 'rbac-mgr' FROM principals p
WHERE p.id IN ( /* list */ ) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM role_assignments rr WHERE rr.principal_id = p.id AND rr.role = 'kms-access');
COMMIT;
```
mira: also add an audit-log entry tag for the backfill so we can filter: `migration_rbac_v3_backfill=1`
miguel: noted. we should also check Cloud Audit Logs for the window 17:50-18:10 for any deleted IAM bindings to confirm scope.
oncall: running preflight checks: verifying DB dump for canary shard, snapshot created 1802504400 (do not delete).
kevin: planning to run backfill at +5m after snapshot verified. will also run `gcloud iam roles describe` and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` for the affected projects to ensure there are no higher-level binding removals.
elain: while we fix data, we should also add a circuit-breaker in the migration to auto-abort if KMS errors exceed 5/min across canary.
mira: good call. I'll open a quick PR to add the rate check and a config flag.
miguel: after backfill, let's run a small load test hitting KMS decrypt with a few sample SAs to ensure KMS perms restored. sample command: `gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=prod --key=primary --ciphertext=... --project=redwood-prod`
oncall: update: snapshot verified and uploaded to s3://redwood-snapshots/1802504400.sql.gz. green to proceed in 2m.
kevin: backfill applied. logs: `UPDATE 42` and `INSERT 0` . added audit tag `migration_rbac_v3_backfill=1`.
miguel: running KMS sanity now. first 10 decrypts succeeded. monitoring for 10 more minutes.
elain: resuming canary in paused mode (no new shards) and will monitor rate. please keep watch on latency and kms_error rate in dashboard.
mira: created PR: https://git.redwood/infrarbac/pull/472 - adds null-check and circuit-breaker threshold. tests added.
oncall: alert rule suppressed temporarily for this thread: kms-heavy-errors Until: 1802505200 by mira.
kevin: postmortem notes to collect: timeline, root cause (null role_map_version assumption), mitigation (backfill + patch), follow-ups (add unit test around nulls, add canary thresholds, update runbook). I'll start the doc.
elain: thanks all. after 30m of stable KMS calls we'll resume full rollout.
miguel: small heads-up — audit logs show one admin user removed binding around 17:58 due to a manual cleanup earlier this week. adding that to the postmortem because it made triage more confusing.
mira: filing infra ticket to add an invariant check to the role mapping generator: deny any prune that would drop both kms-access and fallback_kms for a principal.
oncall: runbook note appended: "on RBAC migration failures that touch KMS, snapshot DB, backfill kms-access, and pause rollout".
kevin: tagging: @sre-runbook-bot please include runbook update in release notes.
sre-runbook-bot: acknowledged. added entry to runbook_changes queue id RBAC-2026-77.
elain: wrapping up. thanks team.
